request: Audio precedes camera/screen/reliable data at the endpoint; no relay media priority. Current focus is excessive video degradation, with strict 200ms acoustic target deferred.
fixes: Group camera no longer jumps to one fps when the Opus controller reports a completed transient concealment/catch-up. The shared ladder and generic source budget handle that evidence. Hard outgoing pressure still forces real secondary yield before longer audio packets.

Otherwise healthy isolated soft loss pauses bounded growth and preserves already earned healthy credit; it cannot repeatedly restart a twelve-second ramp. Actual loss, buffer pressure and unknown/marginal samples retain resets.
Group fixture now hashes full RGBA frames, records native decode sequences and rates, rejects negative buffer-capacity results, and rejects old prefix-hash captures as motion evidence.
Fixture receiver aggregation uses production buffer and outage constants. Captured source proofs include the image helper and transient loss policy.

verified.regressions: Controller 150kbps/15fps -> 10kbps/1fps on one transient was reproduced and fixed. Recovery under isolated events every nine seconds stayed at level 3 on old policy and reached level 0 with the bounded ramp after the fix.

remaining: Video quality in the three-participant constrained relay test is still inadequate: last-minute decode rates 1.37-1.92fps, 80x60 or 120x90. No overall video improvement is claimed.

Every remaining observed ladder reduction in the final capture was a repeated soft audio event. Own receive-side counter windows around two local events contained only about 11/27ms non-silent concealment in six seconds; peer event amounts are not available in the Dart stats yet. Use duration/severity evidence before changing this sensitivity.
Motion and decode counters do not prove screen presentation. Physical camera/headset/speech, screen load, and compatibility/ordered transport performance remain outside these captures.
scope: Three independent SDK/media worker processes, a blind FIFO relay path at 1024kbit/s, 360 measured seconds, six directions and three encrypted files. Separate source selection remains endpoint-local; no relay changes were made.
